dossier.public_summary: The 1.05-day dip matches the star's own 1.048-day spin almost exactly and occurs on a star that varies by 2-3% from spots, with a brightness swing as large as the dip itself. The dip's length and depth change between sectors far more than a planet should, and it is best explained as a spot-crossing modulation, not a transiting planet. No nearby eclipsing star can produce it given the on-target centroid.

reasons.why: Large periodic brightness swing outside the dip, comparable to the dip depth (118% of depth) with very high chi2, the signature of stellar pulsations/close binary or variability, not a planet transit.

Signal period is essentially exactly one stellar rotation period (ratio 0.999) with very large spot/variability amplitudes (10-30k ppm), and the dip is long (3.58 h) vs central 1.171 h for the TIC M dwarf (ratio 1.699, ~523.7 star-density penalty), consistent with rotation-modulated dips not transits; duration fits Gaia radius 0.678-0.68 Rsun (ratio 1.26) not TIC 0.5029.
